title: Applied Materials Posts Record $9.12 Billion Quarter, Edges Past Wall Street Estimates
excerpt: The world's largest chipmaking equipment supplier reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $9.12 billion and earnings of $3.50 per share, beating consensus estimates as AI-driven demand for semiconductor manufacturing tools continues to surge.
body:
• Applied Materials reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $9.12 billion, above the consensus estimate of $8.99 billion, representing roughly 25% year-over-year growth.
  • Adjusted earnings came in at $3.50 per share, beating the $3.40 consensus by $0.10.
  • The results reflect surging demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment driven by AI chip production, high-bandwidth memory, and advanced packaging.
  • Shares have doubled year-to-date but pulled back nearly 30% from June highs, making the earnings report a key test of the AI hardware narrative.

Record Revenue on AI Chip Boom

Applied Materials delivered record quarterly revenue of $9.12 billion for its fiscal third quarter ended August 2026, the company reported Thursday. The result edged above the Wall Street consensus estimate of $8.99 billion and represented approximately 25% growth from the same period a year ago.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $3.50, topping the consensus forecast of $3.40 by a dime. The company had guided for Q3 revenue of $8.95 billion at the midpoint, with adjusted EPS of $3.36, making the beat on both metrics a positive signal for the semiconductor equipment sector.

AI Spending Drives the Cycle

The results underscore how deeply Applied Materials is embedded in the current AI investment cycle. The company's deposition, etch, and inspection tools are essential to manufacturing the advanced chips that power data centers, AI training workloads, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) modules.

Chipmakers including TSMC, Samsung, and Intel have been spending heavily to expand production capacity for AI-related chips, directly benefiting equipment suppliers like Applied Materials. The company's Semiconductor Systems division, its largest segment, has seen particularly strong demand for tools used in advanced logic and memory production.

"We see clearer evidence that equipment companies are raising pricing to drive margins higher."

— UBS analysts, in a recent note hiking their AMAT price target to $705

Stock Has Doubled, Then Pulled Back

Applied Materials shares have roughly doubled in value since the start of 2026, touching a record high of $739.67 in late June. But the stock has since pulled back nearly 30% from that peak, trading around $535 ahead of the earnings release.

The pullback reflected broader concerns about whether the AI hardware spending cycle could sustain its pace, along with questions about the company's free cash flow — which has missed expectations in four of the last five quarters even as earnings beat estimates. That divergence has been a recurring investor concern.

In after-hours trading, shares moved lower despite the beat, suggesting that investors may have been looking for a stronger outlook or more definitive commentary on demand trends heading into 2027.

Analyst Outlook Remains Bullish

Wall Street remains broadly positive on Applied Materials. Ten of 12 analysts tracked by Visible Alpha rate the stock a buy, with an average price target of $689 — implying more than 30% upside from recent levels. UBS recently raised its target to $705, citing pricing leverage across the semiconductor equipment sector.

The company's forward earnings are expected to grow roughly 34% next year, from $12.22 to $16.40 per share, driven by continued expansion of AI chip manufacturing capacity and growing demand for advanced packaging technologies.

What's Next

Applied Materials is scheduled to hold its earnings conference call Thursday at 4:30 p.m. ET. Investors will be listening closely for guidance on the fiscal fourth quarter and management's outlook for 2027 demand, particularly as the market tries to gauge whether the current pace of AI infrastructure spending is sustainable.
